races.name: Racing To School Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap Stakes (Part Of The Racing Excellence Series)

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: A confirmed front runner from the P-style column who gets to lead without a fight here; James Owen's 8/48 14-day record is modest, but the horse's straightforward tactical role is the key asset — uncontested pace-setting over 1m½f on good-to-firm is exactly its scenario, though its finishing kick once headed is the question mark.|

runners_data.name: Popeye Doyle
runners_data.note: Form shows a second over 8f at this venue, but nothing in the profile suggests ability to pick up off a slow gallop; Finlay Bassett's 7lb claim can't compensate for a hold-up style in a race where the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to cause the front end to crack.|

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground under Shay Farmer's patient ride and the 10f trip on today's turf looks well within range; a natural P-style runner who should secure a seat just behind the leader, making him ideally positioned if the race unfolds as a sprint for home — the trainer's 1/7 14-day strike rate is modest but the form string includes recent placing at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Bay Dream Believer
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground this campaign (1 from 5 on good, 4 wins in total on the going) but the H-style is compromised when the gallop is pedestrian; Kyle McHugh's 3lb claim helps at the weights but genuine hold-up horses need a true pace to exploit, and OR 60 from the bottom of the weights is the limit of the upside here.|

runners_data.name: Sceptic
runners_data.note: True hold-up operator — Ian Williams places him here off 34 days, with the visor retained and a course-flat profile — but his natural rear-of-field berth is squeezed into the midfield map because Popeye Doyle and Bay Dream Believer occupy similar ground; his best going is soft/standard, making good-to-firm a marginal concern and the sim-going record (0W from 4 runs) underlines the issue.|

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose recent form includes wins and places over 8-9f on good ground, but the field density at the front pushes her into a midfield slot that blunts her effectiveness; Jake Dickson retains the ride and the 12/15 sim-going record is the strongest in the field, so she retains tactical interest if she can recover ground from a less-than-ideal pitch.|

races.paceDynamic: No Knee Never is the lone confirmed front runner and, with no genuine pressure likely to materialise from rivals, is set to control a sedate, uncontested gallop over this 1m½f trip at Nottingham on good-to-firm turf. Tees George and Perfidia carry prominent profiles but the field holds more pace-minded types than can realistically all track the leader — Tees George, with his course-compatible profile, is best placed to secure a position just off the front, while Perfidia is likely to be shuffled wider into a midfield berth that does not suit her natural game. The resulting shape — one unchallenged front runner, a sustainable tempo, and a muddled mid-group — classically sets up runners with strong finishing kicks launched from a handy position rather than true hold-up horses who need a truly genuine gallop to reel leaders in. Bay Dream Believer and Popeye Doyle, genuine hold-up types, face the steepest task in a steadily-run affair; the tactical verdict favours prominent-to-midfield operators who can travel into contention without being dragged into an early duel, and who possess the turn of foot to pounce on a slow-motion leader through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If No Knee Never dictates a steady, uncontested pace and the race is decided by a sprint in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: No Knee Never sets sail alone at a comfortable tempo, and the winner emerges from horses who have tracked closely and conserved energy throughout; a prominent position is the golden ticket here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mid-Pack Pouncer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a handy-tracked horse quickens past the tiring leader at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A steady pace over 1m½f allows a horse sitting third or fourth to coast into striking distance and pick off the front runner in the final stages; the profile that wins here is a classier mover who has not been drawn into fighting for early position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically mid-race creating a bunched finish that plays into a finisher's hands.
scenarios.body: A compressed final-furlong sprint narrows the gap between styles and gives Bay Dream Believer or Popeye Doyle a slender route through, though both must overcome the fundamental disadvantage of a slow early tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Rises, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected surge of pressure in the middle mile turns the race into a true slog and the field spreads out under duress.
scenarios.body: Horses with genuine stamina and a high cruising speed relative to their rivals benefit when others crack from an elevated gallop; in a six-runner handicap with few genuine pressure-merchants this scenario is the least probable.

watchPoints.text: No Knee Never holds the pivotal tactical key — if it bowls along uncontested at a dawdle, the entire race outcome tilts toward those directly behind it, and any horse that misjudges the early pace risks being left with too much to do.

Perfidia's redistribution from a natural prominent position to midfield is the biggest structural risk — if Jake Dickson pushes forward and the horse actually grabs a prominent berth, Scenario A shifts heavily in her favour and the odds may not reflect it.

Tees George's trainer Adrian Nicholls fires at just 1/7 over 14 days, and the six-year-old has had mixed results stepping back up in trip — if the horse fails to travel comfortably in behind the leader, it could capitulate rather than challenge.

The entire field is racing on good-to-firm at Nottingham yet the race header lists going as GOOD — confirm the actual strip conditions at the course, as Bay Dream Believer's four wins on good ground could be a more potent asset than currently priced if the ground is riding faster than declared.

Sceptic's visor is retained after a second last time out at 8f on good, but today's 12f trip on quick ground is uncharted territory for a horse whose best figures have come on softer surfaces — any sign of the horse struggling to settle in the first half-mile would be a significant negative signal.

races.name: Racing Tv Profits Returned To Racing Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Watch Race Replays At Racingtv.com Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Double Naughty
runners_data.note: Recorded a win at 6f on good ground 15 days ago and arrives in fair recent form, but her natural instinct is to come from well off the pace — in a race with this many hold-up types, she is unlikely to secure as deep a position as she needs and her redistribution to midfield reflects genuine crowding at the rear rather than a change of style.

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Two wins from five starts at 5f and 6f suggest she handles this trip, and the headgear (p) applied here may sharpen her early; however, her hold-up style means she will need a gap to appear in the final furlong on a flat 5f track where the lead has not been burned up.

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: A veteran of 15 similar-ground runs with two wins and five places, she races prominently and knows her job — her course experience at Nottingham is a positive, but the drop back to 5f from recent 6f and 7f starts is a slight concern about whether she truly stays competitive at this sharper trip.

runners_data.name: Sound And Vision
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning from a 189-day absence, and that long layoff is a real flag; she was last seen finishing fifth at Southwell, so Ed Walker has had time to get her straight, but her ability to sustain the gallop for a full 5f on good-to-firm after nearly six months off demands monitoring.

runners_data.name: Control Room
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win and two seconds from her last three starts, racing prominently and clearly in form; her two placed efforts on good ground at 5f suggest this trip and going suit, and Grace Harris has her primed with a 21-day gap since last run.

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 5f trip on good ground just two months ago and arrives the freshest hold-up type in the field at only 13 days since her last run; Tim Easterby's 8-from-73 trainer strike rate over 14 days is modest, but the horse's proven course profile at this distance and going makes her the most credible closer in the field.

runners_data.name: Storm Call
runners_data.note: Wears a visor (v) and has a win on good ground over this 5f trip in her recent history, but is a genuine hold-up horse squeezed toward midfield by the sheer volume of closers in this race — she arrives 11 days fresh and has enough pace for 5f, though her style-fit concern is real given she cannot race as deeply off the pace as she naturally would.

races.paceDynamic: Sound And Vision is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Starsong and Control Room as genuine prominent rivals, she is likely to secure an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over this sharp Nottingham 5f. Starsong and Control Room will press for the early positions just off the leader, creating an honest but not frenetic pace that suits those racing close to the speed. The hold-up contingent — Marajito, Zoustar Dreams, Double Naughty and Storm Call — will need to close from off the pace, but on a flat 5f track with no significant test in the final furlong, the lack of a true end-to-end burn makes it harder to make up ground from deep. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track Sound And Vision and produce a challenge in the final 100 yards; hold-up horses face a stiff task generating the momentum needed to reel in the pace setters. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Double Naughty and Storm Call are true off-the-pace runners shuffled into midfield on the map, and of the two, Storm Call with her recent good-ground form is best placed to try to secure a forward enough berth if the pace relaxes momentarily.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sound And Vision Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sound And Vision crosses cleanly and establishes a clear, uncontested lead from the off, setting a measured but accurate gallop.
scenarios.body: She dictates every inch of the race from her low draw, keeping the fractions honest enough to sustain and making the prominent horses behind her work hard to bridge the gap in the closing stages. Control Room and Starsong are best positioned to pounce on her if she ties up, but against a horse who sets her own tempo this profile strongly benefits those who have been tracking the pace throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Sound And Vision sets a slightly stronger pace than expected, leaving her vulnerable in the final furlong to a horse that has tracked just off the speed.
scenarios.body: Control Room has twice finished second when close to the pace and Starsong holds multiple placed efforts at course-and-distance trips; either is primed to capitalise on a leader who has led from a long way out. This scenario rewards horses that have been travelling comfortably two lengths off the front and can produce a clean finishing effort in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or a bunched field creates a wall that allows a hold-up horse an unusually clear passage through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Marajito has won at 5f on good ground and arrives fresh on 13 days rest with a solid profile at this trip; Zoustar Dreams has course form and front-foot win form that can translate to a late run if the gaps appear. However, the flat nature of the Nottingham 5f and a sustainable pace make this scenario genuinely against the grain for true closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If a messy break sees pace horses check each other and the race devolves into a sprint from the two-furlong pole with no clear order.
scenarios.body: Storm Call and Double Naughty, both natural hold-up horses, could benefit from a compressed field where their finishing speed is suddenly relevant over the last furlong. This is a low-probability shape on a flat, galloping 5f track with a clear pace hierarchy already established.

watchPoints.text: Watch Sound And Vision's break from the stalls — after 189 days off, if she misses the kick or fails to establish her natural lead within the first furlong, the entire race shape collapses and the prominent trackers inherit the advantage immediately.

Monitor Control Room's early positioning — she has the form profile to win if she can sit directly behind Sound And Vision, but if Starsong or another runner forces her wider or back further than ideal, her chance is compromised.

Marajito is the hold-up horse most worth tracking through the race given her proven win over this exact course, distance and going — if she travels sweetly in midfield and a gap opens inside the final furlong, she poses the most credible late threat to the pace horses.

With Double Naughty and Storm Call both genuine off-the-pace types competing for the same limited space at the rear of this small seven-runner field, watch for either or both being bustled along sooner than preferred to avoid being trapped on the rail or blocked in the straight.

races.name: Steve Yarborough Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Poor Relation
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's three-year-old has been racing prominently but her recent form over shorter trips on Soft shows limited conviction — stepping up to 1m2f on Good to Firm is a fresh question, and the STYLE_FIT flag means her mapping into a lead role could flatter her chance slightly if the faster surface suits closer types.

runners_data.name: Crimson Rambler
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with a consistent placing record on Good ground, most recently third and second over 8f, and the step to 1m2f looks like it could play to his strengths; the 5lb claim of Liam Wright is a small asset but the trainer's 0/1 in the last 14 days is not a positive.

runners_data.name: Del Corso
runners_data.note: Ed Walker sends out a horse with an undefined style whose last five runs suggest he travels well and places consistently at 8f on Good — the step to 1m2f is the main question, though his sim-going record of 0W3P from seven attempts means he has rarely won but stays competitive; Ashley Lewis (5) adds some value.

runners_data.name: Miss Pretty
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood and ridden by Harry Davies, this filly won over 7f on Soft but has finished third and tenth over 1m2f on Good, suggesting the trip and going combination can expose her limitations; the trainer's 0/4 in 14 days is a cold angle and she is likely to run prominently without quite holding that position all the way home.

races.paceDynamic: Poor Relation is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-horse field and, with no rival willing or able to press her, she will set a solo, unchallenged gallop from the outset over 1m2f on Good to Firm ground at Nottingham. Miss Pretty maps prominently alongside or just behind her, but neither Crimson Rambler nor Del Corso carries the profile to force the issue, leaving the tempo entirely in Poor Relation's hands. The result is a controlled, honest pace rather than a searching one — the kind of tempo that gives the leader every chance to control the race but also allows hold-up and midfield horses a relatively steady early clip to travel within themselves. This race shape most favours a prominent or hold-up horse with a strong finishing kick, since the uncontested pace means the leader may be vulnerable to a closer who has conserved energy, but it equally rewards any horse capable of racing prominently and quickening from a sensible position once the real racing begins from the home turn.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Poor Relation dictates a calm, untroubled gallop and the small field produces no sustained challenge until deep in the straight.
scenarios.body: Poor Relation sets her own fractions, avoids a battle, and arrives at the home turn with a lead and petrol to burn; in a four-runner race with no pressuring rival, a capable prominent horse is rarely pulled back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Reels Leader In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough that the hold-up horse Crimson Rambler can pick off a tiring leader in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Crimson Rambler travels wide without cover but saves enough for a late run; if Poor Relation has done slightly too much work up front, the hold-up style proves the winning edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Del Corso, whose undefined running style allows versatility, tracks the leaders and quickens at the right moment on the flat Nottingham straight.
scenarios.body: Del Corso's recent form shows consistent placing ability at 8f and the step to 1m2f suits a horse who can travel midfield and accelerate; Ed Walker's yard has decent recent form and Ashley Lewis rides with experience of the trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Duel Saps Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Pretty pushes forward aggressively early and turns the race into a genuine two-way battle for the lead, burning out both lead contestants.
scenarios.body: A contested pace would expose any stamina limitations in Poor Relation and Miss Pretty, collapsing the front end and handing a late winner the race; however, with Miss Pretty wearing a hood and a modest record in similar going, this scenario depends on an unlikely aggressive ride.

watchPoints.text: Watch Poor Relation's early sectionals — if she opens up a two-length lead by the halfway mark unchallenged, she becomes a serious winning proposition given the absence of any pace pressure in this field.

Crimson Rambler's jockey Liam Wright (5) has the least experience in the race and if he settles too far back early in a slow-run four-runner heat, the gap to the leader could prove too large to bridge in the short Nottingham straight.

Miss Pretty's hood could prompt a forward break, and if she contests the lead with Poor Relation she risks burning out both horses and handing the race to the hold-up runners — monitor her early position at the start.

Del Corso's trip record is worth tracking — all five recent runs have been at 8f or 9f, so this is comfortably the longest he has been asked to run; if he weakens in the final furlong it will confirm the trip is beyond him at this stage.

Going description lists the 7:33 race as Good to Firm rather than Good — any horse who has shown a preference for softer conditions, particularly Crimson Rambler whose sim-going record is built on Good, should be observed for signs of the faster surface blunting their finishing effort.

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing Tv Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Racedays For £9 At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ablon
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Richard Hannon and Callum Rodriguez; won over 7f on Standard going recently and has a consistent pattern of tracking the pace — this trip and Good to Firm ground are untested in winning form but his style fits this race shape well.

runners_data.name: Woodstock City
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer for Ian Williams, off 40 days and last seen in a non-handicap context; has a win on Standard over 11f and a place on Good but historically inconsistent, and the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to allow him to close from the rear on this good-ground surface.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed pace-setter and will dictate every yard if left alone; tagged with a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 suggesting this role is actually outside its most comfortable mode, so monitor whether it sustains the gallop all the way to the line or weakens inside the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Didaar
runners_data.note: Trained by Gihan Arnolda with a sharp T14 strike rate of 3/6; won last time out over this exact trip on Good ground and carries just 132lbs — the most compelling form in the race at the weights and the leading hold-up threat if he gets a clear passage.

runners_data.name: Caelan
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's runner arrives just four days after his last run and is a natural hold-up horse over staying trips (his history runs to 17f), making this 1m2f on fast ground a potential concern for stamina use of pace rather than sheer lack of it; pushed forward on the race map but will likely settle further back than shown.

runners_data.name: Revelio
runners_data.note: Has form figures of 2 and 6 on Good ground over 10f and shaped with promise last time for Tom Clover and Harry Davies; a genuine hold-up type displaced into the mapped midfield by an overcrowded rear, so his chances depend on pace being strong enough to make his late run meaningful — the STYLE_FIT tag tempers expectations.

races.paceDynamic: Everyoneknowsadave is the lone confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 1m2f handicap and, with no genuine rival to push the pace, is positioned to control proceedings from the off at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground. Ablon will look to track closely in second, meaning the race is likely to be run at a steady-to-honest tempo rather than a truly searching pace, favouring those who can travel comfortably near the speed. The hold-up contingent — Woodstock City, Didaar, Caelan, and Revelio — will be hunting for a strong enough gallop to make late ground, but the redistribution note is critical: Caelan and Revelio are natural hold-up horses shuffled into the mapped midfield because the true rear of the field is overcrowded, meaning they are unlikely to achieve their preferred positions cleanly. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the controlled pace and produce a sustained finish, rather than genuine closers who need a fast-run race to reel in rivals.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Everyoneknowsadave dictates an uncontested lead and Ablon tracks comfortably, allowing the front two to quicken clear in the straight.
scenarios.body: Everyoneknowsadave sets a fair but unforced gallop and the hold-up horses simply lack the acceleration to close the gap on Good to Firm ground over a trip that rewards rhythm and stamina. Ablon, racing prominently for Callum Rodriguez and Richard Hannon, is ideally positioned to pounce if the leader ties up, making this the dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and one of the genuine closers finds a clear run to pick up late.
scenarios.body: Didaar, who won last time on Good ground over this exact trip and is proven over 10f in this going, is the most plausible beneficiary given his course-relevant form and low weight. Woodstock City has previously won over 11f on Tapeta and could hit the line hard if the leaders burn themselves slightly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Caelan or Revelio manage to find a better position than their redistribution suggests and the pace collapses in the straight.
scenarios.body: Both are true hold-up horses mapped forward on the race diagram, so this scenario depends on them racing outside their natural style — a meaningful obstacle. Revelio's recent second on Good ground over 10f gives him credentials if he can travel prominently, though his STYLE_FIT discount makes this an unlikely unfolding.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Everyoneknowsadave is outpaced or pulled up unexpectedly and the race degenerates into a sprint from 2f out.
scenarios.body: With no other natural front-runner, a pace collapse would produce a muddling contest resolved by a sharp turn of foot, which the modest field ratings suggest is unlikely to produce a conclusive winner. Ablon's recent form figures include a win at this sort of distance and he would adapt best to a changed tempo.

watchPoints.text: Everyoneknowsadave — if it fails to sustain the gallop past the 2f pole, the entire race shape unravels and the hold-up horses gain far more time than the scenario probabilities suggest.

Didaar — the shortest gap since last run (14 days) combined with a sharp Arnolda yard could make him a live danger if he travels easily in midfield; his recent win on this exact trip and going is the standout form line.

Caelan — running just four days after his last start and likely to be further back than the map shows; if he fails to get competitive quickly on the faster ground, his stamina-oriented profile over longer trips is wasted here.

Revelio and Caelan are both true hold-up horses who will be competing for the same late-race ground — watch whether either finds a clear run through the small six-runner field in the straight or whether they impede each other's progress.

Ablon's weight of 134lbs is joint-highest in the race — monitor whether he travels kindly into the straight tracking Everyoneknowsadave or becomes outpaced when the pace lifts, as his recent form over 10f on Good showed a fifth-place finish.
